en: to go on a field trip; to visit; to tour

examples.en: The students are touring a factory.
Last week we visited a museum on a field trip.
Next month we will tour a broadcasting station.
I toured the company and talked with a staff member.
The children touring the farm look happy.

examples.ko: 신문사를 견학해서 기사가 어떻게 만들어지는지 알았어요.
examples.en: I toured a newspaper company and learned how articles are made.

explain: 공부나 일에 도움이 되도록 공장, 박물관, 회사 같은 곳에 가서 직접 보고 배울 때 써요. 그냥 구경하러 갈 때는 '구경하다'를 써요. '견학을 가다'처럼도 말해요.

phrases.en: We are going to tour the factory.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-러 가다'로 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -러 가다 pattern states the purpose of going.

phrases.en: We have an on-site field trip tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 곳이나 실제 장소를 직접 보러 가는 학습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A learning trip to see a real workplace or site.

phrases.en: I applied for a museum tour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 견학은 미리 신청하는 경우가 많아서 이 말을 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Tours are often booked ahead, so this phrase is common.

explain_en: Use it when you visit a factory, museum or company to see and learn firsthand. For just sightseeing, use '구경하다'. You can also say '견학을 가다'.

examples.en: The meeting date hasn't been decided yet.
The wedding venue was decided at today's meeting.
The representative is decided by a vote.
Once the price is decided, I'll let you know right away.
There is one thing that will be decided today.
The exam date was set, so I started studying.

explain: '결정하다'는 내가 정하는 것이고, '결정되다'는 결과로 정해진 상태예요. 말할 때는 '정해지다'가 더 자주 들리고, '결정되다'는 뉴스·공지·회의처럼 공식적인 자리에서 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The meeting place has been set.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결정되다'보다 부드럽고 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than '결정되다' and more common in speech.

phrases.example: 이미 결정된 일이라서 바꿀 수 없어요.
phrases.en: It's already been decided, so I can't change it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 '이미 정해진 일'을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies a noun to mean something already settled.

phrases.en: Please let me know once the date is decided.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'과 함께 어떤 일이 정해진 뒤에 부탁할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-(으)면', it's often used to ask for something once a decision is made.
phrases.en_equiv: let me know once it's decided

explain_en: '결정하다' is you deciding; '결정되다' is the state of having been settled. In speech '정해지다' is heard more, while '결정되다' is common in news, notices and meetings.

dis.h: general word for something being decided
gh: made final and confirmed, no more changes
formal; decided by a group vote

p.n: 확정 means the date is now final and confirmed, not just decided.

t90.ax: The representative is decided by a vote.

examples.en: If you turn the street corner, my house is right there.
A small bakery opened on that street corner.
We decided to meet at that street corner tomorrow.

examples.ko: 길모퉁이 가게 아주머니가 항상 인사해 주세요.
examples.en: The lady at the corner shop always greets me.

examples.ko: 길모퉁이 쪽에서 갑자기 자전거가 나와서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A bicycle suddenly came out from the corner and startled me.
Shall we walk slowly as far as the corner?

explain: 길이 꺾이거나 만나는 바깥쪽 모서리 부분을 말해요. 그냥 '모퉁이'라고도 하고, 좁은 길인 '골목'과는 달라요. '모퉁이를 돌다'처럼 이동하는 동사와 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Turn right at the corner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '길모퉁이'보다 짧고 말할 때 더 자주 써요. 길을 안내할 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than 길모퉁이 and more common in speech; it fits well when giving directions.

phrases.en: Let's meet at the street corner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when deciding on a meeting place.

phrases.en: I bought milk at the shop on the street corner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게의 위치를 설명할 때 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to modify a noun when describing where a shop is.

explain_en: It is the outer corner where a street bends or meets another. People also just say '모퉁이', and it is different from '골목', a narrow alley. It pairs well with movement verbs, as in '모퉁이를 돌다'.

examples.ko: 매운 닭발을 시켜서 친구와 나눠 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ordered spicy chicken feet and shared them with a friend.

examples.ko: 닭발은 처음 먹어 봤는데 생각보다 맛있어요.
examples.en: I tried chicken feet for the first time and they're tastier than I expected.

examples.ko: 저는 닭발이 너무 매워서 물을 많이 마셨어요.
examples.en: The chicken feet were so spicy that I drank a lot of water.

examples.ko: 닭발에는 뼈가 많아서 먹기 조금 불편해요.
examples.en: Chicken feet have lots of small bones, so they're a bit hard to eat.
After work I met a friend at a chicken feet restaurant.
One order of chicken feet to go, please.

explain: 한국에서는 보통 아주 매운 양념으로 볶아서 먹어요. 그래서 '매운 닭발', '닭발집'처럼 자주 말하고, 인기 있는 음식이지만 처음 먹는 사람에게는 낯설 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Spicy chicken feet go well with beer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국에서는 보통 매운 양념으로 먹어서 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In Korea it's usually eaten spicy, so the two words go together.

phrases.en: We got together at a chicken feet restaurant after work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 닭발을 파는 식당을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A restaurant that sells chicken feet.

phrases.example: 저는 닭발을 먹을 때 물을 많이 마셔요.
phrases.en: I drink a lot of water when I eat chicken feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식은 '먹다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Food goes with the verb 먹다.

explain_en: In Korea they are usually stir-fried in a very spicy sauce, so you often hear '매운 닭발' and '닭발집'. It is a popular dish, though it can feel unfamiliar the first time.

examples.en: An eagle draws a big circle in the sky.
Eagles have very good eyesight.
I saw an eagle for the first time at the zoo.
I want to fly high like an eagle.
Please do not feed the eagle.

examples.ko: 산 위로 독수리 한 마리가 날아갔어요.
examples.en: An eagle flew over the mountain.

explain: 일상에서는 영어 eagle처럼 두루 쓰지만, 새 이름으로는 죽은 동물을 먹는 vulture에 가까워요. 비슷한 큰 새로 '매'와 '수리'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 저는 아직 독수리 타법으로 글을 써요.
phrases.en: typing slowly with one or two fingers
phrases.nuance_ko: 자판을 손가락 한두 개로 찾아 치는 모습을 농담처럼 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking way to describe hunting for keys and typing with one or two fingers.

explain_en: In daily talk it is used broadly like 'eagle', but as a bird name it is closer to a vulture that eats dead animals. Similar big birds are 'mae' (hawk/falcon) and 'suri' (eagle).

en: to be foolish; to be stupid; to be idiotic

examples.en: That behavior is a little silly.
I felt like a fool.
It's a silly question, so I'm embarrassed.
The goofy look when you laugh is cute.
He may look foolish, but he has a warm heart.
I think my mistake last time was foolish.

explain: '바보스럽다'는 말이나 행동이 어리석어 보일 때 써요. 친한 사이에서는 귀엽고 어설프다는 뜻으로도 쓰지만 남에게 쓰면 기분 나쁠 수 있으니 조심하세요. '바보 같다'와 비슷하고, 내 모습에 쓰면 부드러워요.

phrases.example: 그 모자를 쓰면 좀 바보스러워 보여요.
phrases.en: You look a bit silly in that hat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 어리석어 보일 때 써요. 남에게 말하면 기분 나쁠 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks foolish; it may sound rude to others.

phrases.en: I was being foolish.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바보스럽다'와 비슷하고, 내 모습에 쓰면 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, and softer when used about yourself.

phrases.en: That question is not foolish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어리석지 않다고 부정할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying something is not foolish.

explain_en: 바보스럽다 is used when words or actions look foolish. Among close people it can mean cute and clumsy, but said to others it can offend, so be careful. It is close to 바보 같다, and it sounds gentler when used about yourself.

examples.en: Who serves first?
I serve with my left hand.
That player served hard.
Next time I'll serve.
Just toss the ball and serve.
It's fine to serve slowly.

explain: '서브를 넣다'와 같은 동작이고, 말할 때는 '서브를 넣다'를 더 자주 들어요. '서브가 좋다', '서브가 약하다'처럼 명사도 자주 써요. 서브를 받는 쪽은 '리시브하다'나 '받다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I will serve first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서브하다'보다 말할 때 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Heard more often in speech than 서브하다.

phrases.en: Now it's your turn to serve.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순서를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about whose turn it is.

phrases.en: Throw the ball high and try serving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시도해 보라고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to suggest trying it.

explain_en: It is the same action as '서브를 넣다', which you hear more often in speech. The noun is also common, as in '서브가 좋다' (good serve) and '서브가 약하다' (weak serve). The receiving side uses '리시브하다' or '받다'.

examples.en: The alien in the movie came to Earth.
Do aliens live somewhere in space too?
Is there anyone who has seen an alien?
The child drew a picture of an alien.
He wore strange clothes like an alien.
I read a story about becoming friends with an alien.

explain: '외국인'과 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 외국인은 다른 나라에서 온 사람이고, 외계인은 지구 밖에서 온 존재예요.

phrases.en: I watched a movie with aliens in it on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 만화 이야기를 할 때 자주 붙는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about movies or cartoons.

phrases.en: I believe in aliens.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외계인이 정말 있다고 생각하는지 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about whether you think aliens really exist.

phrases.en: You look like an alien in that outfit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모습이나 행동이 특이할 때 장난으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used jokingly when someone's look or behavior is unusual.

explain_en: It sounds close to 'oegugin' (foreigner), so learners mix them up. A 'oegugin' is a person from another country; an 'oegyein' is a being from outside Earth.
